claim: Caenorhabditis elegans was the first multicellular organism in which genetic code expansion was established
source: Caenorhabditis elegans was the first multicellular organism in which genetic code expansion was established, and the incorporation of ncAA has been demonstrated in multiple C. elegans tissues (Greiss and Chin, 2011; Parrish et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Greiss and Chin, 2011; Parrish et al., 2012)

claim: The incorporation of ncAA has been demonstrated in multiple C. elegans tissues
source: Caenorhabditis elegans was the first multicellular organism in which genetic code expansion was established, and the incorporation of ncAA has been demonstrated in multiple C. elegans tissues (Greiss and Chin, 2011; Parrish et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Greiss and Chin, 2011; Parrish et al., 2012)

claim: PylRS is localised predominantly to the nucleus when expressed in eukaryotic cells due to a stretch of positively charged amino acids in the N-terminal domain
source: When expressed in eukaryotic cells, PylRS is localised predominantly to the nucleus due to a stretch of positively charged amino acids in the N-terminal domain, which is interpreted as a nuclear localisation sequence by the eukaryotic nuclear import machinery.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about PylRS localization in eukaryotic cells

claim: Addition of a strong nuclear export sequence (S-NES) to the PylRS N-terminus significantly increases the efficiency of ncAA incorporation in mammalian cells
source: Accordingly, addition of a rationally designed strong nuclear export sequence (S-NES) to the PylRS N-terminus was reported to significantly increase the efficiency of ncAA incorporation in mammalian cells by increasing the amount of cytoplasmic PylRS (Nikić et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Nikić et al., 2016)

claim: The S-NES::PCKRS::GFP fusion localised to the cytoplasm
source: As expected, the S-NES::PCKRS::GFP fusion localised to the cytoplasm, while unmodified PCKRS::GFP was almost entirely nuclear, reflecting that the S-NES was able to efficiently shift PCKRS localisation from the nucleus to the cytoplasm (constructs 'no NES' and 'S-NES' Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claim: Unmodified PCKRS::GFP was almost entirely nuclear
source: As expected, the S-NES::PCKRS::GFP fusion localised to the cytoplasm, while unmodified PCKRS::GFP was almost entirely nuclear, reflecting that the S-NES was able to efficiently shift PCKRS localisation from the nucleus to the cytoplasm (constructs 'no NES' and 'S-NES' Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claim: All tested NESs achieved nuclear export of the synthetase PCKRS
source: All tested NESs achieved nuclear export of the synthetase PCKRS (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claim: The p120cts-NES variant reduced incorporation efficiency below the level of unmodified PCKRS
source: However, the NES variants differentially affected incorporation efficiencies: when we co-expressed NES::PCKRS variants with tRNA(Pyl) and the GFP::mCherry incorporation reporter, we found that the p120cts-NES variant reduced incorporation efficiency below the level of unmodified PCKRS, whereas the PKIα-NES and the Smad4-NES robustly increased PCK incorporation efficiency (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: The PKIα-NES and the Smad4-NES robustly increased PCK incorporation efficiency
source: However, the NES variants differentially affected incorporation efficiencies: when we co-expressed NES::PCKRS variants with tRNA(Pyl) and the GFP::mCherry incorporation reporter, we found that the p120cts-NES variant reduced incorporation efficiency below the level of unmodified PCKRS, whereas the PKIα-NES and the Smad4-NES robustly increased PCK incorporation efficiency (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: The presence of the C15 variant significantly increased incorporation efficiency
source: We found that the presence of the C15 variant significantly increased incorporation efficiency (Figure 2C, E, F and G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C, E, F, G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C

claim: The Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) and PKIα-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) pairs improved incorporation efficiency by more than 50-fold compared to the unmodified PCKRS/tRNA(Pyl) pair
source: Compared to the unmodified PCKRS/tRNA(Pyl) pair, the Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) and PKIα-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) pairs improved incorporation efficiency by more than 50-fold; from <0.1% to 4.6% and 4.4%, respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F

claim: Cre recombinase can be photocaged by replacing K201 with PCK
source: Cre recombinase can be photocaged by replacing K201, a lysine residue in the Cre active site, critical for enzyme activity, with PCK (Gibb et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2016; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Gibb et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2016) and illustrated in Figure 3A and B

claim: PC-Cre has previously been expressed in both mammalian cell culture and zebrafish embryos using transient transfection and direct mRNA/tRNA injections
source: PC-Cre has previously been expressed in both mammalian cell culture and zebrafish embryos using transient transfection and direct mRNA/tRNA injections (Luo et al., 2016; Brown et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Luo et al., 2016; Brown et al., 2018b)

claim: Using the optimised Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) expression system, expression of the target locus was observed in 63% of animals 24 hr after uncaging
source: Using the optimised Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) expression system, we observed expression of the target locus, indicative of PC-Cre photoactivation, in 63% of animals 24 hr after uncaging.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the study

claim: No red fluorescence was seen without UV treatment
source: We saw no red fluorescence without UV treatment.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: The 63% activation rate was a vast improvement relative to the 1% observed with unmodified PCKRS and tRNA(Pyl)
source: The 63% activation rate was a vast improvement relative to the 1% we observed with unmodified PCKRS and tRNA(Pyl) (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D

claim: The percentage of full-length protein is between 4% and 5% when using the improved Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) incorporation system
source: As assessed with the GFP::mCherry incorporation reporter, we show that the percentage of full-length protein is between 4% and 5% when using the improved Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) incorporation system (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F

claim: Target gene activation was significantly improved from 63% for PC-Cre to 97% for optPC-Cre
source: When we compared optPC-Cre to PC-Cre, we indeed found that target gene activation was significantly improved: from 63% for PC-Cre to 97% for optPC-Cre (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D

claim: No expression of the ChR2::mKate2 target gene was seen without PCK or UV activation
source: We saw no expression of the ChR2::mKate2 target gene without PCK or UV activation (Figure 3D and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and F

claim: Clear reversals were observed in worms expressing ChR2::mKate2 in the presence of the ChR2 cofactor all-trans-retinal (ATR) when exposed to 470 nm blue light
source: When we exposed worms to 470 nm blue light to activate ChR2, we observed clear reversals in worms expressing ChR2::mKate2 in the presence of the ChR2 cofactor all-trans-retinal (ATR).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: In animals expressing ChR2::mKate2 in the absence of ATR, no reactions were observed
source: In animals expressing ChR2::mKate2 in the absence of ATR, we did not observe such reactions (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Video 1 and Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Video 1 and Video 2

claim: Optogenetic activation of neurons expressing ChR2 from the glr-1p promoter induces backward movement
source: The induced behaviour concurs with previous studies showing that optogenetic activation of neurons expressing ChR2 from the glr-1p promoter induces backward movement (Schultheis et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Schultheis et al., 2011)

claim: The strongest and most robust responses were seen in strains where optPC-Cre was used to control expression of ChR2::mKate2
source: When we compared strains expressing PC-Cre and optPC-Cre, respectively, we saw the strongest and most robust responses in the strains where optPC-Cre was used to control expression of ChR2::mKate2, followed by strains using non-optimised PC-Cre, but using the efficient Smad4-NES::PCKRS/tRNA(C15) incorporation system.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental comparison

claim: Animals expressing unmodified PCKRS and non-optimised Cre showed almost no response to optogenetic activation
source: Animals expressing unmodified PCKRS and non-optimised Cre showed almost no response to optogenetic activation (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C

claim: C. elegans has six mechanosensory neurons for the perception of soft touch: AVM, ALML, ALMR, PVM, PLML, and PLMR
source: C. elegans has six mechanosensory neurons for the perception of soft touch: AVM, ALML, and ALMR, which are located in the anterior of the worm, and PVM, PLML, and PLMR, which are located in the posterior (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans mechanosensory neurons and illustrated in Figure 4A

claim: Worms respond with backward movement to an anterior touch, and with forward movement to a posterior touch
source: Worms respond with backward movement to an anterior touch, and with forward movement to a posterior touch (Chalfie et al., 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Chalfie et al., 1985)

claim: Optogenetic activation of the anterior neurons AVM and ALM results in reversals
source: Previous studies using targeted ChR2 illumination in individual animals likewise showed that optogenetic activation of the anterior neurons AVM and ALM results in reversals, while activation of the posterior neurons PVM and PLM results in forward movement.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from previous studies

claim: Activation of the posterior neurons PVM and PLM results in forward movement
source: Previous studies using targeted ChR2 illumination in individual animals likewise showed that optogenetic activation of the anterior neurons AVM and ALM results in reversals, while activation of the posterior neurons PVM and PLM results in forward movement.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from previous studies

claim: Concurrent activation of all six touch neurons results in reversals in the majority of cases
source: Concurrent activation of all six neurons results in reversals in the majority of cases.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from previous studies

claim: Repeated activation of touch neurons leads to a reduced response due to habituation
source: Repeated activation leads to a reduced response due to habituation (Leifer et al., 2011; Stirman et al., 2011; Schild and Glauser, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Leifer et al., 2011; Stirman et al., 2011; Schild and Glauser, 2015)

claim: Chrimson::mKate2 expression was only present in laser-targeted cells after 12–24 hr
source: After 12–24 hr, we observed Chrimson::mKate2 expression that was only present in laser-targeted cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: Selective activation of optPC-Cre in both PLM neurons, as well as in PLML or PLMR alone, was achieved
source: We were able to selectively activate optPC-Cre in both PLM neurons, as well as in PLML or PLMR alone (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C–E

claim: The presence of the PCK incorporation machinery and optPC-Cre did not affect the function of the touch sensory neurons
source: We confirmed that the presence of the PCK incorporation machinery and optPC-Cre did not affect the function of the touch sensory neurons by assaying the animals response to soft touch (Chalfie et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D

claim: Illumination of animals expressing Chrimson::mKate2 in both PLM neurons triggered a robust response with the worms initiating forward movement
source: We found that illumination of animals expressing Chrimson::mKate2 in both PLM neurons ('2PLM') triggered a robust response with the worms initiating forward movement (Figure 5A,B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Video 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and Video 3

claim: Mock-treated animals grown on PCK and ATR but without activation of optPC-Cre showed no response
source: Conversely, mock-treated animals ('0PLM') grown on PCK and ATR but without activation of optPC-Cre showed no response (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Video 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Video 4

claim: Animals expressing Chrimson::mKate2 only in the PLML or the PLMR neurons respectively showed a clear reaction to stimulation
source: Animals expressing Chrimson::mKate2 only in the PLML or the PLMR neurons respectively also showed a clear reaction to stimulation (Figure 5A,B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Video 5 and Video 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Video 5 and Video 6

claim: A gradual reduction in the response with increasing number of stimulations was observed for all three expression patterns (2PLM, PLML, PLMR), consistent with habituation to the stimulus
source: For all three expression patterns (2PLM, PLML, PLMR), we observed a gradual reduction in the response with increasing number of stimulations, both in the fraction of animals responding and in the speed upon stimulation, consistent with habituation to the stimulus (Stirman et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation and citation to prior work (Stirman et al., 2011)

claim: The 2PLM animals responded stronger to stimulation than animals expressing Chrimson::mKate2 in either PLML or PLMR alone
source: We found that the 2PLM animals responded stronger to stimulation than animals expressing Chrimson::mKate2 in either PLML or PLMR alone, both in regard to the fraction of animals responding, and by velocity (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B

claim: PLMR forms chemical synapses connecting it to 10 downstream neurons including the AVA and AVD interneuron pairs
source: PLMR forms chemical synapses connecting it to 10 downstream neurons including the AVA and AVD interneuron pairs, which are involved in driving backward locomotion.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans connectome

claim: PLMR forms gap junctions to PVCR, PHCR, and LUAR
source: In addition to chemical synapses, PLMR also forms gap junctions to PVCR, PHCR, and LUAR.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans connectome

claim: PLML is connected to the touch response circuit exclusively through gap junctions, formed with the interneurons PVCL, PHCL, and LUAL
source: PLML, on the other hand, is connected to the touch response circuit exclusively through gap junctions, formed with the interneurons PVCL, PHCL, and LUAL.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans connectome

claim: PLML does not form any chemical synapses, with the exception of a single connection to HSNL
source: In fact, PLML does not form any chemical synapses, with the exception of a single connection to HSNL, a neuron involved in the control of egg laying.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans connectome

claim: In worms with ablation of both PLM neurons and the single PLMR neuron, a tap stimulus increased backward movement
source: In worms with ablation of both PLM neurons and the single PLMR neuron, a tap stimulus increased backward movement.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from prior studies

claim: Ablating PLML had no effect on the tap response
source: In contrast, ablating PLML had no effect (Wicks and Rankin, 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Wicks and Rankin, 1995)

claim: The 0.1 s, 3 mW/cm2 stimulus was sufficient to elicit a response in animals expressing Chrimson in both PLMs
source: While the 0.1 s, 3 mW/cm2 stimulus was sufficient to elicit a response in animals expressing Chrimson in both PLMs, neither PLML nor PLMR animals reacted, indicating a synergistic effect of PLML and PLMR and the requirement for activation of both neurons to elicit a reaction in response to weak stimuli (Figure 5D–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: Neither PLML nor PLMR animals reacted to the 0.1 s, 3 mW/cm2 stimulus
source: While the 0.1 s, 3 mW/cm2 stimulus was sufficient to elicit a response in animals expressing Chrimson in both PLMs, neither PLML nor PLMR animals reacted, indicating a synergistic effect of PLML and PLMR and the requirement for activation of both neurons to elicit a reaction in response to weak stimuli (Figure 5D–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: There is a synergistic effect of PLML and PLMR and the requirement for activation of both neurons to elicit a reaction in response to weak stimuli
source: While the 0.1 s, 3 mW/cm2 stimulus was sufficient to elicit a response in animals expressing Chrimson in both PLMs, neither PLML nor PLMR animals reacted, indicating a synergistic effect of PLML and PLMR and the requirement for activation of both neurons to elicit a reaction in response to weak stimuli (Figure 5D–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data shown in Figure 5D–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: Animals expressing Chrimson in PLMR showed a robust reaction to stimulation at 14 mW/cm2 and higher
source: When we increased illumination intensity, we saw a striking difference appear between the responses to PLML and PLMR stimulation, respectively. Animals expressing Chrimson in PLMR showed a robust reaction to stimulation at 14 mW/cm2 and higher.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: The response of PLML animals was consistently below that of PLMR or 2PLM animals
source: In contrast, the response of PLML animals was consistently below that of PLMR or 2PLM animals (Figure 5D–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: Only at the highest intensity setting of 74 mW/cm2 did animals of all three expression patterns respond robustly to the stimulus
source: Only at the highest intensity setting of 74 mW/cm2 did we observe animals of all three expression patterns responding robustly to the stimulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: The observed differences in response for PLML and PLMR are not due to differential expression of Chrimson::mKate2
source: The observed differences in response for PLML and PLMR are not due to differential expression of Chrimson::mKate2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), therefore they are likely due to the asymmetric connectivity of the two neurons within the C. elegans nervous system.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3

claim: The observed differences in response for PLML and PLMR are likely due to the asymmetric connectivity of the two neurons within the C. elegans nervous system
source: The observed differences in response for PLML and PLMR are not due to differential expression of Chrimson::mKate2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), therefore they are likely due to the asymmetric connectivity of the two neurons within the C. elegans nervous system.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data and knowledge of the connectome

claim: PLML and PLMR show some redundancy in triggering the tail touch response after strong stimulation
source: We found that PLML and PLMR show some redundancy in triggering the tail touch response after strong stimulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: Using weaker stimuli, only stimulation of both neurons elicits a response, indicative of a synergistic rather than a simply redundant role for PLML and PLMR
source: However, using weaker stimuli, we found that only stimulation of both neurons elicits a response, indicative of a synergistic rather than a simply redundant role for PLML and PLMR.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation and inference

claim: PLML and PLMR make asymmetric contributions to the touch response
source: Interestingly, our results demonstrate asymmetric contributions of PLML and PLMR to the touch response.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: The touch response is controlled by two parallel pathways that rely on gap junctions or chemical synapses, respectively
source: Considering the electrical and chemical connectome of this circuit (Figure 5C), our results are consistent with a model where the touch response is controlled by two parallel pathways that rely on gap junctions or chemical synapses, respectively.
evidence: The claim is a model inferred from experimental results and knowledge of the connectome

claim: The first pathway involves direct connections of both PLM neurons to the PVC interneurons via gap junctions
source: The first pathway involves direct connections of both PLM neurons to the PVC interneurons via gap junctions.
evidence: The claim is part of a model inferred from experimental results and knowledge of the connectome

claim: Activation of the PVCs through gap junctions triggers forward motion
source: Activation of the PVCs through these gap junctions triggers forward motion.
evidence: The claim is part of a model inferred from experimental results and knowledge

claim: The PVCs form connections with forward command interneuron AVB as well as inhibitory connections with backward command interneurons AVA/AVD
source: The PVCs form connections with forward command interneuron AVB as well as inhibitory connections with backward command interneurons AVA/AVD.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans connectome

claim: The second pathway involves chemical synaptic transmission from PLMR onto AVA and AVD, inhibiting backward locomotion
source: The second pathway involves chemical synaptic transmission from PLMR onto AVA and AVD, inhibiting backward locomotion.
evidence: The claim is part of a model inferred from experimental results and knowledge of the connectome

claim: When only PLMR is stimulated, both pathways are activated, resulting in a stronger response
source: Thus, when only PLMR is stimulated, both pathways are activated, resulting in a stronger response, whereas when PLML alone is stimulated only the gap junction pathway is activated, resulting in a weaker response.
evidence: The claim is part of a model inferred from experimental results

claim: When PLML alone is stimulated only the gap junction pathway is activated, resulting in a weaker response
source: Thus, when only PLMR is stimulated, both pathways are activated, resulting in a stronger response, whereas when PLML alone is stimulated only the gap junction pathway is activated, resulting in a weaker response.
evidence: The claim is part of a model inferred from experimental results

claim: The PVCs are connected to each other by gap junctions and may thus act as electrical sinks for signals from the PLMs
source: Unlike the PLMs, the PVCs are connected to each other by gap junctions and may thus act as electrical sinks for signals from the PLMs.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on knowledge of the connectome

claim: Stimulation of both PLM neurons together results in full activation of the gap junction pathway by activating both PVC neurons
source: Stimulation of both PLM neurons together results in full activation of the gap junction pathway by activating both PVC neurons, which, together with the direct inhibition of AVA/AVD by PLMR, results in full activation of the tail touch motor response.
evidence: The claim is part of a model inferred from experimental results

claim: The strong synergistic effect observed with the simultaneous stimulation of PLML and PLMR indicates a requirement for the stimulation of both PVC neurons
source: The strong synergistic effect we observe with the simultaneous stimulation of PLML and PLMR indicates a requirement for the stimulation of both PVC neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental results

claim: C. elegans contains 302 neurons
source: C. elegans contains 302 neurons, for which the physical connectivity has been determined (White et al., 1986).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge and citation to prior work (White et al., 1986)

claim: The physical connectivity of C. elegans neurons has been determined
source: C. elegans contains 302 neurons, for which the physical connectivity has been determined (White et al., 1986).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (White et al., 1986)

claim: Two thirds of the neurons in C. elegans exist in bilaterally symmetric (left and right) pairs
source: Two thirds of the neurons in C. elegans exist in bilaterally symmetric (left and right) pairs, and similar gross morphological symmetries are seen in the nervous systems of many other animals.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge

claim: The optimised ncAA incorporation system will provide the means to introduce a wide range of new chemical functionalities into proteins in C. elegans
source: Our optimised ncAA incorporation system will provide the means to introduce a wide range of new chemical functionalities into proteins, such as crosslinkers, bioorthogonal groups, and post-translational modifications, and serve as a catalyst for new approaches to manipulate and understand cellular biology in C. elegans (Chin, 2017; Davis and Chin, 2012; Nguyen et al., 2018; Lang and Chin, 2014; Young and Schultz, 2018; Zhang et al., 2015; Baker and Deiters, 2014).
evidence: The claim is speculative about future applications, supported by citations to prior work

claim: The optimisation approach is expected to be easily exportable to other organisms
source: Furthermore, since our optimisation approach is based on components that are not specific to C. elegans, we expect that it will be easily exportable to other organisms.
evidence: The claim is speculative about future applications

claim: C. elegans and other organisms have evolved natural surveillance mechanisms to mitigate against the read-through of stop codons
source: Interestingly, C. elegans and other organisms have evolved natural surveillance mechanisms to mitigate against the read-through of stop codons (Arribere et al., 2016), which will also mitigate against any potential effects caused by our system.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Arribere et al., 2016)

claim: The function of the mechanosensory neurons is unaffected by the presence of the orthogonal ncAA incorporation machinery
source: Indeed, we find that the function of the mechanosensory neurons we assay is unaffected by the presence of the orthogonal ncAA incorporation machinery.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: The recombinase activity of photocaged Cre is tightly controlled; the presence of the photocaging group completely blocks activity
source: First, the recombinase activity is tightly controlled; the presence of the photocaging group completely blocks activity and upon photoactivation, highly efficient wildtype Cre is generated.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: Upon photoactivation, highly efficient wildtype Cre is generated
source: First, the recombinase activity is tightly controlled; the presence of the photocaging group completely blocks activity and upon photoactivation, highly efficient wildtype Cre is generated.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation

claim: Following photoactivation, the photocaged amino acid required for amber stop codon suppression can be removed, leaving worms devoid of photocaged Cre for subsequent biological studies
source: Second, following photoactivation, the photocaged amino acid required for amber stop codon suppression can be removed. Thus translation of full-length Cre ceases, leaving worms devoid of photocaged Cre for subsequent biological studies (Maywood et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Maywood et al., 2018)

claim: Photoactivatable Cre is fully compatible with imaging and optogenetic methods that use visible light due to the stability of the photocaging group at longer wavelengths
source: Third, due to the stability of the photocaging group at longer wavelengths, our photoactivatable Cre is fully compatible with imaging and optogenetic methods that use visible light.
evidence: The claim is based on the chemical properties of the photocaging group

claim: LaserTAC is fast and easily enables the preparation of dozens of animals for downstream experiments
source: Switching on gene expression using LaserTAC is fast and easily enables the preparation of dozens of animals for downstream experiments.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experience with the method

claim: Light activation requires only a microscope-mounted laser, generally used for ablation in most C. elegans laboratories, modified to emit light at 365 nm
source: Light activation requires only a microscope-mounted laser, generally used for ablation in most C. elegans laboratories, modified to emit light at 365 nm.
evidence: The claim describes the technical requirements of the method

claim: Generating the required transgenic strains is straightforward and at present involves the introduction of the genetic constructs, followed by genomic integration
source: Generating the required transgenic strains is straightforward and at present involves the introduction of the genetic constructs, followed by genomic integration.
evidence: The claim describes the technical procedure

claim: Once a transgenic strain is made, any combination of neurons targeted by the promoter that was used can in principle be investigated
source: Once a transgenic strain is made, any combination of neurons targeted by the promoter that was used can in principle be investigated.

claim: LaserTAC removes the requirement for the creation of a potentially large numbers of lines by allowing multiple conditions to be investigated using a single strain
source: This removes the requirement for the creation of a potentially large numbers of lines by allowing multiple conditions to be investigated using a single strain.
evidence: The claim is based on the versatility of the method

claim: LaserTAC offers the ability of precise temporal control, which is generally not available using promoter-based systems
source: A further advantage offered by our approach is the ability of precise temporal control, which is generally not available using promoter-based systems.
evidence: The claim is based on the properties of the method

claim: By inserting loxP sites into genomic loci using CRISPR/Cas9, it should be possible to control, at single-cell resolution, the expression of any endogenous protein
source: By inserting loxP sites into genomic loci using CRISPR/Cas9, it should be possible to control, at single-cell resolution, the expression of any endogenous protein, such as neuropeptides, receptors, innexins, proteins involved in synaptic transmission, etc.
evidence: The claim is speculative about future applications

claim: The components employed are functional in other C. elegans tissues
source: Since the components we employ are functional in other C. elegans tissues (Greiss and Chin, 2011) and indeed in other model systems such as zebrafish, fruit fly, mouse, cultured cells, and ex vivo tissues, we anticipate that our method will have broad applicability beyond the nervous system and beyond C. elegans.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Greiss and Chin, 2011)

claim: The method is anticipated to have broad applicability beyond the nervous system and beyond C. elegans
source: Since the components we employ are functional in other C. elegans tissues (Greiss and Chin, 2011) and indeed in other model systems such as zebrafish, fruit fly, mouse, cultured cells, and ex vivo tissues, we anticipate that our method will have broad applicability beyond the nervous system and beyond C. elegans.
evidence: The claim is speculative about future applications
